# Apollo Advising

> Apollo Advising (Apollo RE Advising LLC) is an hourly real estate consulting firm for rental property owners across the United States. Founder Denver McClure, a Marine Corps veteran and active Texas landlord, helps first-time investors, early-stage landlords, and retirees decide whether to buy, hold, sell, refinance, change rental strategy (short-term, medium-term, long-term), or pursue a 1031 exchange on a property.

## Key facts
- Pricing: $199 per hour, or $499 for a three-hour block used within 12 months. Time is billed in 15-minute increments. The first 30-minute call is free.
- Written option, no call needed: a Rental Property Analysis Report on one property, $99 for a PDF within 2 business days or $149 for rush delivery within 1 business day, with a code for 50% off the first one-hour strategy session, good for 30 days after delivery. Order at https://www.apolloadvising.com/property-analysis/
- Sessions are by phone or Zoom, nationwide. Book at https://www.apolloadvising.com/book/
- Scope: real property and business operations only. Apollo Advising does not provide legal, tax, investment, insurance, or lending advice, and does not advise on securities such as Delaware Statutory Trusts (DSTs), REITs, TIC interests, private placements, or syndications.
- Investment advice is offered only through Nashional Independent Investment Management LLC, a separate registered investment adviser.
- Contact: denver@apolloadvising.com

## Short answers
- Should I sell my rental property or keep it? Compare keeping, selling, and exchanging side by side, starting with return on equity: annual net cash flow divided by market value minus loan balance. Example: a $450,000 rental with a $150,000 loan netting $9,000 a year earns 3% on its $300,000 of equity, before appreciation and loan paydown.
- What are the 1031 exchange deadlines? 45 days after the sale closes to identify replacement property in writing, and 180 days to close (sooner if the tax return is due first, unless extended). A qualified intermediary must hold the proceeds.
- Airbnb, medium-term, or long-term rental? Compare net income after all costs and the time each takes. Short-term usually has the highest gross and highest costs; furnished stays of 30+ days often land in between.
- Does Apollo Advising give investment advice? No. Investment advice is offered only through Nashional Independent Investment Management LLC, a separate registered investment adviser.

## Decisions (short answers)
### Should I buy this rental property?
Buy a rental only when the numbers still work with realistic rent, vacancy, repairs, capital expenses, and reserves, and when the property fits a strategy you have time to run. The cheapest moment to catch a bad deal is before the offer, which is why a one-hour review pays for itself so often.
Source: https://www.apolloadvising.com/buying-a-rental-property/
### Should I keep my rental property, sell it, or do a 1031 exchange?
Compare three paths for the same property: keep it, sell it, or exchange it. Start with what your equity is earning each year, then weigh the taxes a sale would trigger, the time the property takes, and what you would do with the money. Once all three sit side by side, the answer is usually clear.
Source: https://www.apolloadvising.com/hold-sell-or-1031-exchange/
### Should I refinance or take equity out of my rental property?
A refinance, cash-out refinance, or HELOC is worth exploring only when it serves a specific goal and still leaves the property with healthy cash flow and reserves. Doing nothing is often the best option, so compare it first.
Source: https://www.apolloadvising.com/refinance-and-equity-decisions/
### Should my rental be a short-term, medium-term, or long-term rental?
Compare net income, not gross revenue. Short-term rentals usually earn the most per night and cost the most to run. Long-term leases earn the least and take the least time. Furnished medium-term stays of 30 days or more often land in between. Local rules and your own time decide the rest.
Source: https://www.apolloadvising.com/rental-strategy/
### What should I do with my rental properties in retirement?
Look at each property on its own. Keep the ones that earn their keep with little of your time, simplify the ones that do not with management or a strategy change, and consider selling or exchanging the rest. The goal is predictable income and a workload you are comfortable with.
Source: https://www.apolloadvising.com/retirees-and-long-time-landlords/

## Frequently asked questions
### About Apollo Advising
Q: What does Apollo Advising do?
A: Apollo Advising is an hourly real estate consulting firm. We help rental property owners and buyers work through a specific decision: whether to buy a property, keep or sell one, refinance, change rental strategy, or pursue a 1031 exchange. We provide research, analysis, and a clear view of the tradeoffs. You make the decision.
Q: Who is Apollo Advising for?
A: First-time investors buying their first rental, early-stage landlords with one to a few properties, and retirees or long-time owners deciding whether to keep, simplify, or sell their rentals.
Q: Do you work with property owners outside Texas?
A: Yes. Sessions are by phone or Zoom and we work with clients across the United States. Denver's own rental properties are in Texas, and the analysis methods apply to any U.S. market.
Q: Who is Denver McClure?
A: Denver McClure is the founder of Apollo Advising. He is a Marine Corps veteran and an active Texas landlord who has used house hacking, ADU conversions, and short-term, medium-term, and long-term rental strategies in his own portfolio. He founded Apollo Advising in 2023.
Q: How is this different from a real estate agent or property manager?
A: Agents are usually paid when a transaction happens, and property managers are paid to run the property. Apollo Advising is paid by the hour for analysis, whether you buy, sell, or do nothing. Denver does hold interests in affiliated firms, which are listed on our disclosures page.
### Pricing and scheduling
Q: How much does it cost?
A: $199 per hour, or $499 for a three-hour block that you can use within 12 months. The first 30-minute introductory call is free.
Q: Can I get a written analysis without a call?
A: Yes. The property analysis report covers one property in a written PDF: $99 for delivery within 2 business days, or $149 for delivery within 1 business day. You answer an intake form instead of booking a call, and the PDF comes with a code for 50% off your first one-hour strategy session, good for 30 days after delivery. Start at the property analysis page.
Q: Do I pay for a full hour if we finish early?
A: No. Time is billed in 15-minute increments, so a 45-minute session is billed as three quarters of an hour.
Q: What counts as billable time?
A: Meetings, plus work done for you outside of meetings: research, financial modeling, spreadsheets, written reports, recorded video walkthroughs, review of documents you send, and substantive correspondence. Anything expected to take more than an hour is estimated in advance and not started without your approval.
Q: What is your cancellation policy?
A: Cancel or reschedule at least 24 hours ahead and the time goes back to your balance. Missed sessions are charged as used.
Q: What should I bring to my first session?
A: The property address, purchase price and date, current loan balance and rate, current or expected rent, 12 months of income and expenses if you own it, and what you want the property to do for you over the next few years.
### Common decisions
Q: Should I sell my rental property or keep it?
A: It depends on how much equity is tied up, the cash flow after realistic reserves, the taxes a sale would trigger, how much time the property takes, and what you would do with the money instead. We model the keep, sell, and exchange scenarios side by side so you can compare them, and give you the tax questions to confirm with your CPA.
Q: Is a 1031 exchange worth it?
A: Sometimes. A 1031 exchange can defer capital gains tax when you sell investment real estate and buy like-kind property, but it comes with strict deadlines (45 days to identify replacement property and 180 days to close) and you take on a new property and often new debt. We help you weigh the tradeoffs and timing and prepare questions for your qualified intermediary, CPA, and attorney. We do not act as an intermediary.
Q: Should I convert my Airbnb to a long-term or medium-term rental?
A: Compare net income after all costs, not gross revenue. Short-term rentals often earn more on paper but carry higher cleaning, furnishing, platform, and management costs, more vacancy risk, and local ordinance risk. We compare short-term, furnished medium-term, and long-term scenarios for your specific property and market.
Q: Can you help me decide whether to refinance or take out a HELOC on a rental?
A: Yes, at a strategic level. We look at whether a refinance, cash-out refinance, or HELOC is worth exploring given your goals, and what each would mean for cash flow, reserves, and flexibility. Apollo Advising does not originate, broker, or recommend specific loans or lenders.
Q: I'm retired and own rental properties. Can you help me decide what to do with them?
A: Yes. Many retirees want less work and more predictability. We lay out the options for each property, such as keeping it with professional management, changing strategy, selling, or exchanging, and what each would require, so you can decide with the numbers in front of you.
### What we do not do
Q: Is Apollo Advising an investment adviser?
A: No. Apollo Advising is a real estate and business consulting firm. It does not provide investment, legal, tax, insurance, or lending advice. Investment advice is offered only through Nashional Independent Investment Management LLC, a separate registered investment adviser affiliated with Denver McClure, under its own agreement.
Q: Do you give advice on Delaware Statutory Trusts (DSTs)?
A: No. DSTs are securities, and Apollo Advising does not evaluate or recommend DSTs, REITs, tenant-in-common interests, private placements, or syndications. If you are considering a DST as replacement property in a 1031 exchange, investment advice is available only through Nashional Independent Investment Management LLC, a registered investment adviser, under a separate agreement. Contact Denver to confirm whether that is the right fit.
Q: Do you sell insurance or arrange loans?
A: Not through Apollo Advising. If you need insurance or financing, we can refer you to an affiliated firm or you can use any provider you choose. There is never an obligation to use an affiliate.

## Glossary
### Returns and numbers
- Return on equity: A rental's annual net cash flow divided by its equity, which is today's market value minus the loan balance. It shows what the money tied up in a property is earning now. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#return-on-equity)
- Cash-on-cash return: Annual pre-tax cash flow divided by the total cash you put in to buy the property, including the down payment, closing costs, and initial repairs. It measures the purchase; return on equity measures the property today. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#cash-on-cash-return)
- Cap rate: Net operating income divided by the property's price or current value. Because it ignores financing, it is useful for comparing properties with each other, not for judging your own cash return. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#cap-rate)
- Net operating income (NOI): Rental income minus operating expenses such as taxes, insurance, repairs, management, and vacancy, before mortgage payments, depreciation, and income taxes. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#noi)
- Net cash flow: What a rental leaves you after every operating expense, the full mortgage payment, and a reserve for repairs and capital items. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#cash-flow)
- Gross rent multiplier: Price divided by annual gross rent. A quick screening number that ignores expenses entirely. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#gross-rent-multiplier)
- Appreciation: The increase in a property's market value over time. It is not guaranteed, and it shows up as equity rather than cash until you sell or borrow against it. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#appreciation)
- Loan paydown: The principal portion of each mortgage payment, which reduces the loan balance and builds equity. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#loan-paydown)
### Running a rental
- Vacancy rate: The share of the year a rental sits empty, usually budgeted as a percentage of gross rent. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#vacancy-rate)
- Capital expenditures (CapEx): Large, infrequent replacements such as roofs, HVAC systems, water heaters, and flooring. Owners usually set aside a monthly reserve for them. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#capex)
- Reserves: Cash set aside for repairs, capital expenditures, and vacancy so one bad month does not become a crisis. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#reserves)
- Depreciation: A tax deduction for the wear on a rental building, not the land. Residential rental property is generally depreciated over 27.5 years. Your CPA calculates it. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#depreciation)
### Rental strategies
- Short-term rental (STR): A furnished rental for stays of a few nights, usually booked through platforms such as Airbnb or Vrbo. Many cities regulate stays under 30 days. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#short-term-rental)
- Medium-term rental (MTR): A furnished rental for stays of 30 days to several months, often for traveling nurses, relocating workers, and insurance placements. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#medium-term-rental)
- Long-term rental (LTR): An unfurnished rental on a lease, typically 12 months. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#long-term-rental)
- House hacking: Living in one unit or room of a property and renting out the rest to offset or cover the mortgage. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#house-hacking)
- Accessory dwelling unit (ADU): A second, self-contained living unit on a single-family lot, such as a garage apartment, backyard cottage, or converted basement. Local zoning decides whether one is allowed. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#adu)
### 1031 exchanges
- 1031 exchange: A transaction under Section 1031 of the Internal Revenue Code that lets you defer capital gains tax when you sell investment or business real property and reinvest in like-kind real property. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#1031-exchange)
- Qualified intermediary (QI): The independent party that holds sale proceeds during a 1031 exchange. If the proceeds reach you, the exchange generally fails. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#qualified-intermediary)
- Like-kind property: For real estate, real property in the United States held for investment or business use is generally like-kind to other such property, so a rental house can be exchanged for an apartment building or land. A primary home does not qualify. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#like-kind-property)
- Identification period: The 45 days after the sale closes in which replacement property must be identified in writing. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#identification-period)
- Exchange period: The 180 days after the sale closes in which replacement property must be acquired, ending sooner if the tax return for that year is due first, unless extended. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#exchange-period)
- Boot: Cash or other value received in an exchange that is not like-kind property, including debt that is paid off and not replaced. Boot is generally taxable. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#boot)
- Delaware Statutory Trust (DST): A trust that holds professionally managed real estate and sells fractional interests to investors. A DST interest can generally serve as like-kind replacement property in a 1031 exchange, but it is a security: typically illiquid, with no investor control and fees that vary by sponsor. Consult a licensed investment adviser before investing. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#dst)
- Depreciation recapture: When you sell a rental, the part of the gain that comes from depreciation you took is generally taxed at rates up to 25%. A 1031 exchange can defer it along with capital gains tax. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#depreciation-recapture)
### Financing
- Loan-to-value (LTV): The loan balance divided by the property's value. Lenders use it to set how much you can borrow. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#ltv)
- Debt service coverage ratio (DSCR): Net operating income divided by annual mortgage payments. Many lenders look for 1.2 or higher on rental loans, though requirements vary. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#dscr)
- Cash-out refinance: Replacing your mortgage with a larger one and taking the difference in cash. It raises the balance and usually the payment. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#cash-out-refinance)
- HELOC: A home equity line of credit: a revolving line secured by a property's equity. Lines on investment property are less widely available and usually carry higher rates. (https://www.apolloadvising.com/glossary/#heloc)
